questions.answer: No. Option 0 has no stages and no synchronization, so it is not a legal choice for the Gray pointer crossings and breaks the read margin. It exists only for a flow that inserts the synchronizer outside the IP.

Yes. There is no frequency or ratio restriction. Flags are pessimistic (late to deassert, never early). Latency is S destination edges, up to S+2 with the metastability model, and S depends on the cell option.

The spec says the flags are combinational from the local pointer registers and the synchronized pointer of the other domain, and the Gray register is derived from the next binary pointer. The exact full and empty equations (the MSB-inverted Gray compare or the binary compare) are not written anywhere. The designer must define them.

Yes, the synchronized Gray pointer is converted to binary after the synchronizer. The difference is taken modulo 2 x depth, which is the pointer width. Every LPARA_PTR_W-bit threshold value is accepted. A threshold of 0 makes o_full_thr always 1, and a value above the depth makes it never 1.

The spec says the thresholds are written once before the FIFO is used and do not change while it is in use. It does not define 'in use' (for example after reset release or first access). It also does not define behavior if they change, and no check is specified. The designer must decide.

No. PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE is one parameter shared by all crossings, and option 0 is not a legal option for the pointer crossings of this IP, so a FIFO with option 0 is not legal. The request and acknowledge synchronizers use the same stage count as the pointers, so they get no separate exemption.
A checker shall ignore o_rd_data while o_empty = 1, because its value is the undefined storage content. It shall only check that the value is never X when a read is accepted.

o_full falls at the same write-clock edge at which the write FSM returns to RUN and o_sw_rst_busy is cleared, provided i_rst_n_sw = 1. After that edge the normal full logic applies. Before it, o_full stays 1 because wr_blk = 1.

REQ-SRST-018 is complete in the document. It defines wr_blk = o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0), and o_sw_rst_busy is 0 after the hardware reset i_rst_n_wr (asynchronous clear). The same wr_blk definition is in Section 10.7.2.

The spec defines the assertions on internal signals (wr_blk, rd_blk, FSM state), as in SVA-007 and SVA-008. wr_blk is also expressible at ports as o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0), and o_empty = 1 is a port-level check. Both forms are used.

Yes. Until the request reaches the read domain, the read side is not blocked and o_empty is normal, so it may be 0. Reads in that window are normal reads of pre-reset words. o_empty is forced to 1 only from the cycle the read side is blocked.
Verification shall use legal values only. Behavior with an illegal value is undefined and not checked by the IP.
PARA_AFIFO_MEM_USE_MACRO = 1 enables the library SRAM branch (FEAT-008) and the SRAM macro model (FEAT-010). PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE selects the synchronizer cell option.

The spec gives the values: o_full = 1 and o_empty = 1 while blocked. It also states INV-002 (full and empty never both 1) without an exemption. Both flags are 1 during the software reset, so the spec is inconsistent here. The designer must decide whether INV-002 and SVA-001 are exempt during software reset.

Blocked accesses are not accepted and raise no overflow or underflow pulse. INV-005 and INV-004 are not stated to apply to the software-reset case. The reset itself resets the pointers and discards words, and the spec does not say whether the invariants are suspended. The designer must decide.

Yes. The storage is read every cycle with the next-pointer address, so o_rd_data already shows the new word before o_empty falls. The first read edge after a write may capture an unsettled word, but o_empty falls no earlier than the second read edge, when the word is clean.
o_full is 1 in the same cycle in which i_rst_n_sw = 0 (zero-latency combinational block). o_sw_rst_busy rises only at the next write-clock edge, so busy lags the block by up to one cycle.

Yes. A rejected write leaves the stored data and write pointer unchanged, and a rejected read leaves the read pointer unchanged. o_overflow and o_underflow are registered, non-sticky pulses of exactly one cycle in their own domain (write clock for overflow, read clock for underflow), in the cycle after the rejected request.
Writes are blocked from the same cycle in which i_rst_n_sw = 0, not after the handshake. Reads are blocked from the cycle in which the synchronized request is 1, or while the read FSM is not in RUN.

The spec only says the thresholds are static, written once before use, and not changed while the FIFO is in use. It does not define an observable event or signal for 'in use', and it specifies no testbench check. The designer must define it.

The read side is released first, when the synchronized request is 0 and the synchronized write Gray pointer is 0. The write side is released last, when the synchronized acknowledge is 0 and the synchronized read pointer is 0. The write release needs ack = 0, which is the effect of the read release, so the handshake forces the order.

A hardware reset has priority and resets the FSM and pointers of its domain asynchronously. Resetting both domains gives a clean restart. Resetting one domain only can leave the other waiting forever. The IP does not repair this, and ASM-005 says operation starts only after both domains have left reset.

They differ only in structure. Option 1 is two D-FF cells in series and option 2 is one 2-FF cell. Both have 2 stages, the same function and the same simulation model. The cell choice affects MTBF and the synchronizer cell.

Section 8 lists 'stage count outside 2..4' as illegal, but no stage-count parameter exists (removed by DEC-039). Stages are set by PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE, which also allows 0 stages. The spec does not reconcile this, so the designer must clarify what the stage-count illegality means.

Option 0 is a legal parameter value and gives a bypass (o_q = i_d). It is not legal for the FIFO pointer crossings, where the flag would change in the same cycle as the pointer and the read margin breaks. The IP does not check it, and the wrapper alone is tested for option 0.

They are internal. The top port list has no pointers. The Gray pointers appear only as ports between the wr, rd and mem modules (o_wr_gray, o_rd_gray, i_wr_gray, i_rd_gray). The binary and synchronized pointers are internal signals of wr and rd.

The bound is S destination edges (S = stages of the selected cell: 2, 2, 3, 4). With the metastability model it is up to S+2 edges. The estimate differs from the true occupancy only by pointer updates still inside the synchronizer.
A read blocked by the software reset raises no o_underflow pulse. Only a read of the empty FIFO after the read release gives a normal underflow pulse.
With plain synchronizers o_empty falls S edges after the first capturing edge. With the metastability model it falls at S, S+1 or S+2. The minimum is S >= 2 edges, also for the model.
While blocked, the flags take empty-FIFO values. o_full_thr = 0 (for i_full_thr > 0) and o_empty_thr = 1.

Yes. The block follows i_rst_n_sw combinationally in the same cycle, while o_sw_rst_busy is a flip-flop that rises at the first write-clock edge afterwards. Busy is therefore up to one write-clock cycle behind the block. Software must not use busy = 0 alone while i_rst_n_sw = 0.

Yes, o_full is forced to 1 during the whole write-side block even though the FIFO is empty. There is no conflict: o_full returns to the normal value 0 at the write release, when the FSM returns to RUN and wr_blk falls.
The check is 'empty = 1 while both pointers are 0 after the read release'.

The empty-FIFO value is the threshold formula evaluated at occupancy 0. For i_full_thr = 0 this is occupancy >= 0, so o_full_thr = 1. This matches the general rule that i_full_thr = 0 makes o_full_thr always 1.

Yes. rd_blk becomes active only when the synchronized request reaches the read domain, so a read accepted before that is a normal read of a pre-reset word and does not violate the no-read-while-rd_blk check.
Yes, both are in the prototype checks: after a hardware reset both FSMs are in RUN, both pointers are 0, o_empty = 1 and o_full = 0. A deadlock timeout is also listed.

wr_blk is an internal signal, not a port. It is defined as o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0), both of which are visible at the ports, so R1 and R6 can be asserted either on the internal signal or on that port expression.

If i_rst_n_sw = 0 at the edge where the FSM returns to RUN, busy falls but wr_blk stays 1 because of the input, and o_full stays 1. Writes remain blocked. Busy then rises again one write-clock cycle later when the FSM takes the new request, which is the R8 one-cycle gap.
Only the order is required: the read side returns to RUN before the write side. No minimum delay is specified. The 25 ns in the example is a measured value only.

One write-clock cycle is enough, and any longer hold is allowed. The request is latched at the first write edge where i_rst_n_sw is 0, so it must be low at a sampling edge. A pulse shorter than that is not sampled.

Step (3) says to drive i_rst_n_sw back to 1 'after the reset has started' but does not define how to detect this (o_sw_rst_busy = 1 or a number of cycles). The spec shows that a one-cycle pulse is latched at the first write edge, but it does not name the criterion for software. The designer must define it.
The flags are registered. They are 1 for one clock cycle, in the cycle after the rejected request is sampled at the clock edge.

A write is rejected whenever the registered full flag is 1. A read in the other domain does not free a slot in the same cycle, because the write domain only sees the read pointer after the synchronizer latency.

The spec says an access blocked by the software reset raises no pulse. It does not say whether an overflow or underflow pulse already due from a rejected request just before the block begins is suppressed or still shown. The designer must decide.

S is the stage count of the cell selected by PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (2, 2, 3, 4 for options 1 to 4). Flags are combinational from the synchronized pointer, so the nominal latency is S destination edges. With the metastability model it is up to S+2, so the S to S+2 range is the permitted spread. It applies to both flags: o_empty deasserts after a write, and o_full deasserts after a read.
Yes. Option 0 is tested only for the wrapper alone (latency 0 and reset value). FIFO-level tests use options 1 to 4.

A value above 4 is illegal and its behavior is undefined, so it is not verified. Verification uses legal values only. The statement that the wrapper then gives the 4-FF cell is only the implementation of the undefined case.

Re-assertion in REL keeps writes blocked and starts a new sequence when the FSM is back in RUN. A hardware reset has priority over the software reset and resets the FSM and pointers of its domain. Resetting both domains gives a clean restart. Resetting only one domain leaves the other waiting, and this is not repaired.
SVA-014 requires both FSMs to return to RUN within a 'bounded number of cycles', but no numeric bound is given. The designer must define it.
The EXC-003 value is 1 x the period of the receiving clock i_clk_rd. Only EXC-001, EXC-002, EXC-005 and EXC-006 use 0.9 x the source period.

The flags are not sticky. They self-clear after one cycle, and the hardware reset also clears them. There is no clear input or register. 'Recovery by user logic' means the producer or consumer reacts to the flags, with no retry or drain provided.

The condition is that the project policy uses set_clock_groups. In that case the bounded-delay constraints and the CDC analysis shall cover the crossings separately. The IP owns the crossing constraints.

The technology cell option is the parameter PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (0 to 4), which selects the cell by wrapper parameter. The macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS only selects the synthesis or simulation branch of the wrapper. It is checked in simulation for each option, in both branches.

A value above 4 is illegal and its behavior is undefined (not checked), even though the wrapper happens to give the 4-FF cell. Option 0 on the pointer crossings is not a legal use of the IP and is not checked. It is tested only at wrapper level.

There is no separate stage parameter. DEC-039 removed PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_STAGE, and S is set by PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (default 2, giving 2 stages). The metastability latency therefore depends on S through the cell type.

The estimate is not exact at a given instant. It is pessimistic: the full side can read larger than the true occupancy and the empty side smaller. It differs from the true occupancy only by pointer updates still inside the synchronizer, which means S to S+2 edges with the model. No numeric tolerance is given beyond that.

Read-data correctness is checked by SVA-004 (scoreboard: a read returns the word written to that entry) and by a no-X check on accepted reads. The pointer protocol keeps the data stable regardless of the per-bit latency, with EXC-003 bounding the path. No separate stability assertion is listed.
DEC-042 replaces DEC-040. The example cells keep the library pin names CK, RN or SN, D, Q and are exempt from the naming rule.
The macro model returns the old word on a same-edge read and write. The wrapper's simulation branch that returned X was removed by DEC-043, so the testbench checks the old-word behavior.

The full and empty flags are pessimistic, meaning they can be late to deassert but never early. The threshold flags are also derived from the synchronized pointer and are pessimistic. The lateness is up to S destination edges nominally and up to S+2 with the metastability model. No almost-full or almost-empty flags exist beyond the threshold flags.
